activities.caption: file each loop: amplifier or stabiliser
activities.name: estpLoopsBuckets

config.prompt: The atmosphere's feedbacks — file each loop:

items.label: water vapour — warmer air holds more, and it is itself a greenhouse gas
ice–albedo — melt exposes dark ocean, which absorbs more heat
permafrost carbon — thaw releases CO₂ and methane, causing more thaw
the Planck response — thermal radiation grows steeply with temperature

config.why: The system's character is the race between them: for small forcings the stabilisers win; near thresholds an amplifying loop can take over and change becomes self-driving.

activities.anchor: supplies the candidates, each with a mechanism
activities.caption: pair each tipping element with its mechanism
activities.name: estpElementsMatch

config.prompt: Six named candidates — pair element with mechanism:

pairs.right: marine ice-sheet instability — deepening bedrock geometry makes retreat self-sustaining
melt-elevation feedback: lower surface, warmer air, more melt
freshening from meltwater weakens the sinking that drives it
deforestation plus drying flips rainforest to savanna
gradual rather than threshold, but self-reinforcing carbon release

config.why: Coral reefs are largely committed already — 70–90% expected lost at 1.5 °C, above 99% at 2 °C. The 2022 Science assessment (Armstrong McKay et al.) rated each element's range and confidence.

activities.anchor: The forest recycles its own rainfall
activities.caption: call the threshold — how much clearing is too much?
activities.name: estpAmazonEstimate

config.prompt: Lovejoy and Nobre argued that beyond a certain share of Amazon deforestation, the basin's hydrology could pass a point of no return. Roughly what share?
config.why: Roughly 20–25% — the southeast, now substantially cleared and already a net carbon source in drought years, sits closest to any such line.
config.context: Fire is the accelerant: degraded, drier forest burns, and burned forest degrades further.

activities.anchor: The assessed reality is mostly thresholds with wide uncertainty bands
activities.caption: true or false — reading the risk honestly
activities.name: estpDoomJudge

statements.s: Climate science says we are already doomed next decade.
statements.why: Most thresholds sit above current warming (about 1.2–1.3 °C), some are being probed now — doom language and denial make the same error.

statements.s: 'Low confidence in the exact threshold' means 'no risk'.
statements.why: Irreversibility is what changes the calculus — this is the tail-risk logic that underwrites precaution.

statements.s: A 10% chance of a permanent, cascading loss is managed differently from a 10% chance of a reversible one.
statements.why: That asymmetry is the whole point: low-probability plus irreversible is a different risk object.

statements.s: Mistaking uncertainty for a conclusion is the shared error of doom and denial.
statements.why: Uncertainty about where a threshold sits is a reason to weigh the tail, not to dismiss it.

activities.anchor: is the syllabus's worked example of a non-linear environmental failure with a happy ending
activities.caption: rebuild the acid-rain arc
activities.name: estpAcidOrder

config.prompt: Detected, crashed, capped, recovered — put the acid-rain story in order:
items: SO₂ and NOₓ oxidise in the atmosphere to sulfuric and nitric acids, deposited wet and dry
Soils and lakes buffer the acid invisibly for decades
The buffering saturates — pH crashes abruptly: fishless lakes, forest decline
1990: the Acid Rain Program caps SO₂ with a fixed, declining, traded allowance total
Emissions fall about half within a decade, far below projected cost — lakes and forests recover
config.why: Threshold problems are detectable, attributable and reversible with sufficient forcing reduction — the template the climate case studies against.

activities.anchor: revealed the shock: polar stratospheric clouds
activities.caption: put the cloud threshold on the thermometer
activities.name: estpCloudPlace

config.prompt: The ozone hole's non-linearity turns on clouds that form only below one critical temperature. Where does it sit?
config.why: Below about −78 °C, polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces that multiply chlorine's reactivity — gradual CFC growth produced an abrupt, deep hole rather than thinning.

activities.anchor: distinct problems sharing a few molecules
activities.caption: find the faulty line — ozone vs warming
activities.name: estpOzoneSpot

config.prompt: A student's comparison contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The ozone hole is stratospheric chemistry: chlorine catalysis, amplified by polar clouds.
Global warming is radiative physics driven mainly by CO₂.
Fixing the ozone hole also fixed the greenhouse effect — same mechanism, same remedy.
CFCs are potent greenhouse gases, so the phase-out helped climate too.
Which is why the ozone remedy could not be copy-pasted onto carbon.
config.correction: They are separate problems: ozone depletion actually cooled the stratosphere slightly rather than warming the surface.
config.why: The equations, the offending gases and the remedies differ — overlapping molecules do not merge the problems.

activities.anchor: not because the alarm was overblown
activities.caption: bet before you read on — why the layer came back
activities.name: estpRecoveryPredict

config.q: The Antarctic ozone layer is projected back to 1980 levels around 2066. Why is it healing?
choices: The threat was imaginary — it healed on its own
A legally binding, near-universal phase-out cut chlorine loads
CFCs turned out to be harmless after all
config.why: Chlorine peaked in the 1990s and declines because the Montreal Protocol is enforced; without it, models project a collapsed ozone layer by the 2050s — environmental successes are evidence that the response works.
